## Goal

Update the canonical MCP dispatch/transport documentation so it records the new
idempotency ownership, cache keying, TTL/eviction, and write-tool retry rules,
keeping the doc in sync with the implemented behavior (REQ-008).

## Scope

- Modify `docs/22_mcp/mcp_03_01_dispatch-and-routing.md` only.
- Covers REQ-008 (documentation only).
- Canonical MCP dispatch/transport doc per `docs/00_index.md`; update its
  "Tool Call Dispatch Flow" section (and adjacent Implementation Notes as needed).

## Assumptions

- The doc must describe behavior AFTER this fix; do not document the pre-fix
  shared-key bug.
- ADR-004/ADR-007 are refreshed only if their wording actually changes as a result
  of this fix (conditional, not mandatory).
- All doc body text stays in English (`skills/DESIGN.md` Output language).

## Design decisions

- Add a concise "Idempotency and retry" subsection under "Tool Call Dispatch Flow"
  covering: key ownership, empty-key rule, cache keying, TTL/eviction, and the
  write-tool retry rule.
- Keep the description behavioral and source-linked (point to
  `dispatch.py` / `http_transport.py`), not a copy of implementation detail
  (content policy: implementation details belong in code, not prose).

## Alternatives considered

- **Rewrite the whole doc:** rejected — scope the change to the dispatch/transport
  flow only; other sections (routing, DAG scheduling, lifecycle) are unaffected.
- **Move idempotency into a new doc:** rejected — REQ-008 targets the existing
  canonical dispatch/transport doc; a new doc would fragment the mcp domain.

## Implementation

### Target file

`docs/22_mcp/mcp_03_01_dispatch-and-routing.md`

### Procedure

1. In the "Tool Call Dispatch Flow" section, add an "Idempotency and retry"
   subsection documenting:
   - **Ownership:** the caller/Agent generates one idempotency key per logical
     call; `HttpTransport.call()` sends it as `X-Idempotency-Key` and reuses the
     same value across that call's retries.
   - **Empty-key rule:** a call without a key (or with an empty/None key) always
     executes and is never cached.
   - **Cache keying:** the server-side dedup cache keys on idempotency key plus
     tool name plus a normalized args hash; key reuse with different content is
     rejected.
   - **TTL / eviction:** the cache carries a TTL and a max-entry bound with
     oldest-first eviction.
   - **Write-tool retry:** write-tool post-send retries occur only when a key is
     present; read-tool retry is unchanged.
2. Reference `scripts/mcp_servers/dispatch.py` and
   `scripts/shared/http_transport.py` as the authoritative implementation.
3. Review ADR-004 and ADR-007; update their references here only if their wording
   changed as a result of this fix.

### Method

- Insert the subsection immediately after the existing "Implementation Notes
  (Current behavior)" bullets (lines 45-49) so it sits within the dispatch flow.
- Match the doc's existing heading hierarchy and cross-link style (see the
  ADR-003 links used throughout).

### Details

- Current doc (lines 26-49) documents `HttpTransport.call()` and dispatch without
  idempotency/cache semantics; the new subsection fills that gap.
- The `X-Request-Id` correlation note (line 28) is unrelated to idempotency and is
  left intact.
